questions.question: What is the event generated by a random variable $X:S\to\mathbb R$ and a set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$?
questions.explanation: The event generated by $X$ and $B$ is the preimage $\{\omega\in S:X(\omega)\in B\}$ — the outcomes whose value lands in $B$.
questions.source_support: The definition gives $\{\omega\in S:X(\omega)\in B\}$.

option_explanations: $\{x\in\mathbb R:x\notin B\}$ is a complement in $\mathbb R$, not a subset of $S$.
$P(X)$ is a number, not an event.
$S\cup\mathbb R$ mixes the sample space with the real line; it is not a preimage.
